info.title: OAS Discriminator Edge Cases
info.description: A comprehensive test spec covering every known discriminator and polymorphism edge case from CX tickets (Sep 2025 - Mar 2026). Each endpoint isolates a specific bug scenario with descriptions referencing the original Linear ticket.

post.summary: CX-2794: Cross-contamination between separate discriminators sharing the same propertyName
post.description: Bug: When two completely separate schemas each define a discriminator with the same propertyName and both include mapping, the renderer incorrectly leaks subschema options from one discriminator into the other. For example, PaymentA's discriminator options (CreditCard, BankTransfer) appear as selectable variants inside PaymentB's discriminator, even though they are unrelated schemas. The mapping entries cause a global lookup by propertyName instead of scoping to the owning schema. Expected behavior: Each discriminator should be scoped to its own schema. PaymentA should only show CreditCard and BankTransfer as variants. PaymentB should only show Crypto and Voucher. The shared propertyName (payment_type) should not cause any cross-contamination between the two independent discriminators.

post.summary: CX-2726: Mapping within discriminator causes an additional level of nesting
post.description: Bug: When a parent schema uses allOf inheritance with a discriminator that includes a mapping object, the renderer introduces an extra, unnecessary level of nesting for each subschema. Removing the mapping (while keeping the same propertyName and oneOf structure) renders correctly with a single level. Expected behavior: The presence of a mapping object in the discriminator should not affect the nesting depth of subschemas. The mapping should only control label-to-schema association (e.g., displaying 'card' instead of 'CardPayment'). Both CardPayment and WirePayment should render with exactly one level of nesting, identical to how they render when the mapping is removed.

post.summary: CX-2725: Discriminator causes additional nesting when nested inside a property
post.description: Bug: When a oneOf with a discriminator is placed inside an object property (rather than at the top level of the request body), the renderer generates two levels of nesting instead of one. The same oneOf + discriminator at the top level renders correctly with a single level. The bug is specifically triggered when the discriminator is nested within a named property of an object schema. Expected behavior: The discriminator inside wrapper.nested_payment should render with exactly one level of nesting — a single dropdown/selector allowing the user to choose between OptionX and OptionY, with their respective fields displayed flat beneath the selection. The nesting depth should be identical regardless of whether the discriminator is at the top level or nested inside a property.

wrapper.description: The discriminator is nested inside this property, which triggers the double-nesting bug

post.summary: CX-2694: Infinite recursion when mapping is defined in a discriminator with allOf
post.description: Bug: When child schemas inherit from a parent via allOf, and the parent schema defines a discriminator with a mapping object, the renderer enters infinite recursion. The child schemas reference the parent via allOf, and the parent's discriminator mapping points back to the children, creating a circular resolution loop. Without the mapping, the same allOf + discriminator structure renders correctly. Expected behavior: The renderer should detect the circular reference between the parent's mapping and the children's allOf and break the cycle. It should render a flat discriminator selector showing Dog and Cat as variants, with each variant displaying the merged properties from both the base schema (animal_type, name) and the child-specific properties (breed for Dog, indoor for Cat). No infinite recursion or stack overflow should occur.

post.summary: CX-2698: Discriminator with inline oneOf schemas only renders the first variant
post.description: Bug: When a oneOf uses a valid discriminator.propertyName with inline schemas (not $ref), only the first schema variant is rendered and all subsequent variants are silently ignored. The same schema structure using $ref instead of inline definitions renders all variants correctly. The discriminator resolution logic fails to iterate beyond the first inline subschema. Expected behavior: All three inline variants (InlineVariantA, InlineVariantB, InlineVariantC) should be rendered as selectable options in the discriminator dropdown, just as they would be if defined via $ref. Selecting each variant should display its unique fields (alpha_field, beta_field, gamma_field respectively). Inline vs $ref should produce identical rendering.

post.summary: CX-2696: discriminator+allOf within discriminator+oneOf/anyOf causes performance issues
post.description: Bug: When a parent schema uses anyOf with a discriminator, and each subschema in the anyOf references another parent schema (which itself has a discriminator) via allOf, the renderer builds a nested accordion for each subschema. With many subschemas this causes severe performance degradation or complete failure to load. Expected behavior: When the outer discriminator+anyOf and the inner discriminator+allOf share the same propertyName, the inner discriminator should be suppressed since the outer one already handles variant selection. The renderer should display a single flat discriminator selector with ClickEvent, PurchaseEvent, and SignupEvent as options. Selecting a variant should show the merged properties (base fields like timestamp plus variant-specific fields like element_id). No nested accordions should be generated, and the endpoint should load instantly.

post.summary: CX-2648: Discriminator nested inside oneOf/anyOf does not render
post.description: Bug: When a schema is structured as a top-level oneOf where one of the subschemas itself contains a oneOf with a discriminator, the inner discriminator is completely ignored and its subschemas fail to render. The renderer only processes discriminators at the top level and does not recurse into nested polymorphic schemas. Expected behavior: The top-level oneOf should present two options: SimpleOption and NestedDiscriminatorOption. When NestedDiscriminatorOption is selected, the nested_choice property should render its own discriminator with InnerOptionA and InnerOptionB as selectable variants. Discriminators should work at any depth of nesting, not just at the top level.

post.summary: CX-2857: Discriminator subschemas containing their own oneOf fail to render
post.description: Bug: When a parent schema defines a oneOf with a discriminator, and one or more of the discriminator's subschemas themselves contain a nested oneOf (for their own properties), the renderer fails to display the nested subschemas. The parent discriminator works, but any polymorphism within a discriminated variant is lost. Expected behavior: The parent discriminator should render EmailNotification and PushNotification as selectable variants. When EmailNotification is selected, the template property should display its own oneOf selector with HTMLTemplate and PlainTextTemplate as options. When PushNotification is selected, the payload property should display AlertPayload and SilentPayload. Polymorphism within discriminated variants should render correctly at all levels.

get.summary: CX-2920: Mapping nested in allOf inside a parent oneOf causes subschema duplication
get.description: Bug: When a response schema uses a parent oneOf, and a subschema within that oneOf is composed via allOf from a base that itself has a oneOf + discriminator + mapping, the parent oneOf duplicates itself as one of its own subschemas. This creates a recursive rendering loop where the parent appears inside its own children. The bug only manifests in response schemas, not request bodies. Expected behavior: The response should render a top-level oneOf with exactly two options: MandateResponseAlpha and MandateResponseBeta. Each variant should display the merged properties from MandateBase (including mandate_type, currency) plus variant-specific fields (alpha_id or beta_id). The inner discriminator (DirectDebit vs StandingOrder) from MandateBase should be handled within each variant, but the parent oneOf should never appear as a duplicated child of itself.

200.description: The response schema triggers the duplication bug

post.summary: CX-2982: Mapping in discriminator causes slow endpoint rendering (minutes)
post.description: Bug: When a discriminator includes a mapping object that references many subschemas, endpoint rendering can take several minutes or become completely unresponsive. The same spec without the mapping (relying on automatic discriminator resolution) renders quickly. The mapping triggers an expensive resolution path that scales poorly with the number of mapped schemas. Expected behavior: The endpoint should render within a few seconds regardless of whether a mapping is present. The discriminator should display all six user role variants (AdminUser, RegularUser, ServiceAccount, GuestUser, BotUser, ApiUser) as a dropdown, and selecting each variant should instantly display its properties. Performance should be equivalent to the same spec without the mapping object.

post.summary: CX-2998: Discriminator field shows all base enum values instead of the resolved value
post.description: Bug: When a base schema defines a discriminator property (e.g. type_id) with a broad enum like [1, 2, 20, 50], and child schemas inherit via allOf and narrow the enum to a single value (e.g. [1]), the UI always displays the full base enum [1, 2, 20, 50] regardless of which variant is selected from the dropdown. Expected behavior: When the user selects 'OptOutEvent' from the discriminator dropdown, the type_id field should display only [1]. When 'OptInEvent' is selected, it should show only [2]. When 'UpdateEvent' is selected, only [20]. When 'DeleteEvent' is selected, only [50]. The child schema's narrowed enum should always override the base schema's broad enum for the selected variant.

post.summary: CX-2727: Mapping to an unused schema renders it as an alternative
post.description: Bug: When a discriminator's mapping references a schema that does not actually participate in the discriminator (i.e., the mapped schema does not reference the parent schema via allOf), that orphaned schema is still rendered as a selectable variant. In this case, Lizard is listed in the mapping but does not use allOf to inherit from AnimalParent, yet it still appears as a selectable option. Expected behavior: Only Dog and Cat should appear as selectable variants, since they are the only schemas that reference AnimalParent via allOf. Lizard should NOT be rendered as an alternative because it does not participate in the discriminator's inheritance hierarchy. A mapping entry pointing to a schema that doesn't inherit from the parent should be ignored.

post.summary: CX-2706: Incomplete mapping object causes unmapped schemas to be ignored
post.description: Bug: When a discriminator's mapping object only defines entries for some of the child schemas (e.g., maps 1 out of 3), the unmapped schemas are completely ignored and not rendered. In this case, only Car (mapped as 'sedan') is shown; Truck and Motorcycle are silently dropped. Expected behavior: All three variants should be rendered. Car should appear with the custom label 'sedan' (from the mapping), while Truck and Motorcycle should appear with their default schema names since they are not in the mapping. Per the OAS specification, a partial mapping provides aliases for some schemas but does not exclude the unmapped ones from the oneOf.

post.summary: CX-3047: Inline oneOf subschemas with mapping causes rendering error
post.description: Bug: When a schema defines a oneOf with inline subschemas (not $ref) and the discriminator includes a mapping object, the endpoint throws a rendering error and fails to load entirely. The same schema structure using $ref instead of inline schemas works correctly. This is a more severe variant of CX-2698 where the addition of mapping escalates the bug from 'only first variant shown' to 'complete rendering failure'. Expected behavior: Both SiteConfigA ('static') and SiteConfigB ('dynamic') should render as selectable variants in a discriminator dropdown. Selecting 'static' should show document_root, selecting 'dynamic' should show origin_url. The combination of inline schemas + mapping should produce the same result as using $ref schemas + mapping. No rendering error should occur.

post.summary: CX-3017: Inconsistent polymorphism rendering between request and response bodies
post.description: Bug: After the polymorphism UI redesign, oneOf/anyOf renders differently in request bodies vs response bodies. The request body uses the new redesigned UI, but the response body still uses the old rendering. Since both use the same underlying feature, this inconsistency confuses users who see different presentations of the same schema structure depending on whether it appears in a request or response. Expected behavior: The exact same schema (CX3017_PolymorphicPayload) is used in both the request and response. Both should render identically using the new polymorphism UI — a discriminator dropdown with JSONFormat and XMLFormat as options, with consistent visual styling, interaction patterns, and layout in both the request body (left panel) and response body (right panel).

requestBody.description: Request body uses the NEW polymorphism rendering

200.description: Response body uses the OLD polymorphism rendering, creating an inconsistency

post.summary: CX-2311: Enum constraints from oneOf subschemas are not applied
post.description: Bug: When a parent schema defines a property with a broad enum, and oneOf subschemas further restrict that property to a narrower set of enum values, the narrowing is ignored. Each subschema instance shows the full parent enum instead of only the values allowed by that specific subschema. For example, the parent allows [CONSENT_RECEIPTS, COOKIE_RECEIPTS, DATA_SUBJECTS] and a subschema narrows to [CONSENT_RECEIPTS], but the UI still shows all three options. Expected behavior: When viewing ConsentExport, the exportType field should only allow CONSENT_RECEIPTS. When viewing CookieExport, only COOKIE_RECEIPTS. When viewing DataSubjectsExport, only DATA_SUBJECTS. Each oneOf subschema's narrowed enum should override the parent's broad enum, restricting the selectable options to only those valid for that specific variant.

post.summary: CX-2990: Array with type: array and oneOf/anyOf items fails to render
post.description: Bug: When a property has type: array and the items schema uses oneOf or anyOf, the entire schema fails to render properly. Arrays that reference polymorphic items are not displayed as expected, and the rendering breaks for the whole endpoint. Expected behavior: The simple_items array should render as an expandable array field. When expanded, each item should present a oneOf selector allowing the user to choose between TextItem and ImageItem. The polymorphic_items array should behave identically using anyOf. Both oneOf and anyOf should work correctly as array items schemas, displaying all variant options and their respective fields.

simple_items.description: An array whose items use oneOf - this combination breaks rendering

polymorphic_items.description: Another array with anyOf items to verify both keywords are affected

get.summary: CX-2956: Blank schema rendering when the same $ref is reused across nested oneOf and allOf
get.description: Bug: When a base schema defines a property using oneOf with a $ref, and a derived schema (composed via allOf from the base) redefines the same property using allOf with the same $ref target, the derived schema renders as blank. The $ref deduplication logic incorrectly treats the reused reference as already resolved, causing the derived schema's properties to be empty. Expected behavior: DerivedSchemaA should render all its properties: base_field (from BaseSchema), derived_a_field, and reused_prop (merged from SharedSchema + extra_a). DerivedSchemaB should render base_field, derived_b_field, and reused_prop (merged from SharedSchema + extra_b). The fact that SharedSchema is referenced in both the base's oneOf and the derived schema's allOf should not cause deduplication — each usage context is distinct.

post.summary: CX-3036: Property values are carried over between oneOf subschemas
post.description: Bug: When switching between oneOf subschemas inside an array, property values persist from the previously selected subschema if the properties share the same name. This occurs when: the oneOf is inside an array, properties have the same names across variants, one of the properties is an enum, and default handling is enabled. For example, selecting 'active' in VariantWithEnum's status enum, then switching to VariantWithString, causes 'active' to persist in VariantWithString's plain string status field. Expected behavior: When switching from VariantWithEnum to VariantWithString, all form values should reset to the new variant's defaults. The status field in VariantWithString should be empty (or its own default), not carry over the enum value 'active' from VariantWithEnum. Each variant switch should produce a clean form state, even when property names overlap between variants.

items.description: Array containing oneOf items where values carry over between variants

post.summary: CX-2675: Subschemas auto-collapse and values reset after request execution
post.description: Bug: When a schema uses oneOf and the user enters values into a selected subschema then executes the request, the subschema automatically collapses. Additionally, entered values are reset when two subschemas contain properties with the same name (both ConfigA and ConfigB have endpoint), because the state management cannot differentiate which subschema the values belong to. Expected behavior: After executing a request, the currently selected subschema should remain expanded and all entered values should be preserved. The user should be able to execute the request, review the response, and continue editing without re-entering values. Values in properties with the same name across variants (like endpoint) should be scoped to the selected variant and not cleared on request execution.

post.summary: CX-2471: Polymorphisms within additionalProperties are not handled
post.description: Bug: When anyOf, allOf, or oneOf is used inside additionalProperties, the polymorphic schema is completely ignored. The renderer does not process polymorphic constructs when they appear within additionalProperties, treating the value as if no schema was defined. Expected behavior: The metadata object should render with additionalProperties that present a oneOf selector for each additional key. Users should be able to add key-value pairs where the value is either a simple string or a structured object with value and source fields. The polymorphic schema inside additionalProperties should be rendered and interactive, just as it would be if used in a regular properties definition.

metadata.description: Object with polymorphic additionalProperties - the oneOf is silently ignored

get.summary: CX-2659: additionalProperties inside polymorphism within array items not rendered
get.description: Bug: When a response schema contains an array whose items use a polymorphic schema (oneOf/anyOf), and the subschemas within that polymorphism define additionalProperties, those additional properties are not displayed. The renderer drops additionalProperties when they are inside a polymorphic schema that is used as array items. Expected behavior: The results array should render each item with an anyOf selector (TypeA or TypeB). When TypeA is selected, it should display kind, name, AND indicate that additional string properties are allowed. When TypeB is selected, it should display kind, count, AND indicate that additional integer properties are allowed. The additionalProperties definition should be visible in the schema documentation regardless of the polymorphic + array nesting context.

200.description: Response with array items using polymorphism + additionalProperties

results.description: Array items using anyOf where additionalProperties are dropped

post.summary: CX-2617: Body Params selection does not sync Request and Response examples
post.description: Bug: When a schema uses oneOf with a discriminator and the user selects a variant in the Body Params section (e.g., choosing 'identity_verification'), the Request and Response example dropdowns on the right side do not update to reflect the same variant selection. Users must manually sync both sides, which is confusing because the dropdowns represent the same set of choices. Expected behavior: When the user selects WorkflowA ('identity_verification') in the Body Params section on the left, the Request example dropdown on the right should automatically switch to show the WorkflowA example, and the Response section should switch to WorkflowAResponse. All three views (Body Params, Request example, Response example) should stay in sync when the user changes the selected variant in any one of them.

200.description: Response that should sync with the selected request variant
